title: Polymorphism instead of instanceof

blocks.text: A chain of `instanceof` checks has to be edited every time a new type appears, and silently ignores a type it does not know. Polymorphism puts the behaviour in each class instead: every `Shape` computes its own `area()`, and code that uses shapes just calls it.
`Shapes` holds `interface Shape { double area(); }` and two records. Complete them:

items: `total(List<Shape> shapes)` returns the sum of the areas, and must work for **any** `Shape`, including kinds added later that you have never seen, so it uses no `instanceof` at all.

cases.says: Circles and rectangles know their areas, and the total adds them.
A Square the solution never saw still counts: total asks each shape for its area.

concepts: Type-specific behaviour is better written as overridden methods than as a chain of instanceof checks.
